home.home.01: Dai Pan is a visual artist based in Brisbane. He works with images and text through photography, printmaking and artist books.
home.home.02: Focusing on light, material and the passage of time, he explores links between everyday scenes, bodily perception and memory.

about.about.01: Dai Pan is a visual artist based in Brisbane, Australia. His practice centres on images and text, working through photography, printmaking and artist books. Conceptual design and design research inform his approach to framing, sequence and material process. He works with the photograph both as an image and as material: a film frame may become a sequence, a lithographic print or part of a handmade book.
about.about.02: His practice moves between poetic realism and post-documentary photography. Informed by phenomenology and East Asian existential thought, his work attends to bodily perception, the physical qualities of objects and the experience of time. Juxtaposition, repetition and pauses bring uncertainty within everyday scenes into view.
about.about.03: Dai Pan is a visual artist based in Brisbane, working with images and text through photography, printmaking and artist books. His practice explores material presence, bodily perception and the experience of time.
about.about.04: Poetry and prose are published at daipan.ink. The Threes (2025), a selected collection of poetry, images and a short narrative, brings writing and book design into a single handmade publication.

contact.contact.01: I welcome collaborations and exhibition opportunities. I’m happy to contribute across visual design, photography and web development, and to explore other ways of working together.

closing_time.closing_time.01: Closing Time (2025) translates a film photograph made in Manhattan into a hand-printed, five-colour photo lithograph. CMYK layers and opaque white soften photographic detail, bringing artificial light, reflections, and surface texture into a painterly image. The work investigates how layered registration changes the clarity and atmosphere of a photographic source.

gallery_design.gallery_design.01: Monolith for Light is a conceptual gallery shaped by the weight of stone and the passage of light. Narrow incisions open the dense volume, admitting daylight onto rough mineral surfaces and into the spaces between them.
gallery_design.gallery_design.02: As the sun moves, illuminated edges and patches of shadow shift across the visitor’s path. The body gives these changes a scale: a threshold invites approach, a bright surface asks for pause, and a dark passage slows the pace of looking.
gallery_design.gallery_design.03: The roof plan, elevation and section relate the faceted stone envelope to the internal rooms and circulation.
gallery_design.gallery_design.04: Separate routes for visitors, artwork handling and service access organise movement through the proposed gallery.
gallery_design.gallery_design.05: The night study retains the mass in deep blue shadow while narrow warm incisions articulate its edges. The exploded view separates roof, enclosure and service level to clarify their spatial relationships.
gallery_design.gallery_design.06: Inside, narrow openings and angled surfaces guide the visitor’s attention. The corridor and daylight studies explore how the same enclosure changes as light shifts over the course of a day.
gallery_design.gallery_design.07: Sectional studies describe the relationship between the interior voids and the surrounding stone mass, setting dark passages against illuminated rooms.
gallery_design.gallery_design.08: The final site study relates the elongated gallery to its approach, orientation and surrounding landscape.

the_threes.the_threes.01: The Threes is a selected collection published in 2025. This handmade artist book brings eighteen poems, abstract images and a short narrative into three sections: Poetry, Image and Story.
the_threes.the_threes.02: Read related poetry and prose at daipan.ink.
the_threes.the_threes.03: Words, geometric drawings and intervals of white space establish the pace of reading, allowing connections to form across the spreads.
the_threes.the_threes.04: Written, designed and assembled independently, the book treats text and image as parts of the same material process. The page becomes a space for memory, reflection and shifts in attention.

reframed_still.reframed_still.01: Reframed Still (2021–2025) is a sequence of gelatin silver photographs made across New York, Guangzhou, Shanghai, and Nantong. The edit brings moments of urban stillness into relation through light, shadow, and composition. Presented as a continuous strip, the sequence invites viewers to compare individual frames and follow the intervals between them.
reframed_still.reframed_still.02: Reframed Still (2021–2025) is a sequence of gelatin silver photographs made across New York, Guangzhou, Shanghai, and Nantong. The edit brings moments of urban stillness into relation through light, shadow, and composition. Presented as a continuous strip, the sequence invites viewers to compare individual frames and follow the intervals between them.

quite_off.quite_off.01: Quite Off began with a script and storyboards, yet remains an unfinished film. Its photographs linger around a suspended beginning: a gaze at close range, a red interruption in a field, a fine web held between leaves.
quite_off.quite_off.02: Family and friendship are approached through closeness and an uncertain presence. A tree holds an interval of stillness within the landscape; a wall turns a coloured surface into a boundary. Red and green carry an emotional continuity across these separate scenes.
quite_off.quite_off.03: A window frames a moment of departure. The sequence returns to a place where the story remains unresolved, leaving absence, memory and what lies outside the frame in tension.

quite_off_mobile.quite_off_mobile.01: Quite Off began with a script and storyboards, but remains an unfinished film. These photographs gather around a narrative that never fully arrives: a gaze at close range, a red interruption in a field, and a web held between leaves.
quite_off_mobile.quite_off_mobile.02: Family and friendship are approached through an uncertain closeness. A face held near the camera can remain difficult to read; a solitary tree can carry the weight of a pause. What connects these scenes is less a shared event than a way of looking.
quite_off_mobile.quite_off_mobile.03: Red interrupts the field of green, then returns as a wall or the trim of a car. Colour carries an emotional continuity through places that remain distinct, holding the unfinished narrative together without resolving it.
quite_off_mobile.quite_off_mobile.04: Windows frame departure without revealing what follows. A road, a passing landscape and the final building become traces of a story outside the photograph. The sequence ends in a place rather than a resolution, leaving memory to continue beyond the last frame.

masks.masks.01: Masks is a limestone lithography series developed in 2024–2025. Drawing on Fumiko Enchi’s Masks (1958), this print treats the face as a changing structure shaped by social relationships. Folded surfaces and gestural marks replace a stable, recognisable identity.
masks.masks.02: This print examines concealment and recognition through fragments of the face. Eyes appear within an abstract structure, holding the image between the desire to remain unseen and the wish to be understood.
masks.masks.03: This print develops curiosity as a pressure on perception. Enclosed, twisting forms bring the desire to look into tension with resistance to being seen; their repeated folds suggest an unstable continuity within the image.
masks.masks.04: Repetition reduces the image to a sustained directional movement. The print brings attraction, obsession, and projection into an abstract structure, allowing their relationships to emerge through repeated viewing.
masks.masks.05: Masks is a limestone lithography series from 2024–2025. Drawing on Fumiko Enchi’s Masks (1958), this print approaches the face through changing surfaces and gestural marks.
masks.masks.06: Fragments of eyes and faces move between concealment and recognition, keeping the image open between remaining unseen and being understood.
masks.masks.07: Enclosed, twisting forms explore curiosity as a pressure on perception and the tension between looking and being seen.
masks.masks.08: Repeated forms gather attraction, obsession, and projection into a sustained directional movement.

in_praise_of_time.in_praise_of_time.01:
In Praise of Time considers photography as a crystallisation of duration. Light, shadow and gesture make bodies, objects and spaces newly perceptible.

Jun’ichirō Tanizaki’s In Praise of Shadows informs this attention to material presence. A passage from Natsume Sōseki’s And Then (1909) places bodily sensation beside an awareness of passing time.

Made in separate settings, these photographs share no continuous event. Juxtaposition, changes of scale and pauses allow correspondences without resolving their uncertainty.
in_praise_of_time.in_praise_of_time.02: In Praise of Time follows the effects of light on bodies, objects and the spaces they occupy. The photographs begin in uncertainty, attending to the brief moments when the material world becomes newly perceptible.
in_praise_of_time.in_praise_of_time.03:
Photography gives passing time a material form. Made in separate settings, these images share no continuous event; their relationships emerge through light, gesture and changes of scale.

Informed by Jun’ichirō Tanizaki’s In Praise of Shadows and Natsume Sōseki’s And Then, the series approaches time through bodily sensation and material presence. The photograph holds an interval while leaving its surrounding life unresolved.

the_threes_mobile.the_threes_mobile.02: Written, designed and assembled independently. Read related poetry and prose at daipan.ink.

gallery_design_mobile.gallery_design_mobile.01: Monolith for Light is a conceptual gallery in which stone, shadow and movement shape the act of looking. Folded planes and narrow openings admit light into a dense enclosure, giving the visitor a changing sense of depth, scale and orientation.
gallery_design_mobile.gallery_design_mobile.02: Inside, rough surfaces catch a narrow wash of daylight. The visitor’s body gives these shifts a scale: a bright edge invites approach; a dark passage slows the pace of looking.
gallery_design_mobile.gallery_design_mobile.03: The drawings connect the faceted envelope to rooms and circulation. Visitor, artwork and service routes are kept distinct, allowing different kinds of movement through the gallery.
gallery_design_mobile.gallery_design_mobile.04: The exploded study separates the roof, enclosure and service level. Material details show how thin openings and angled junctions allow light to interrupt the apparent solidity of the stone.
gallery_design_mobile.gallery_design_mobile.05: The same chamber is held in view at four moments. Changing light makes the passage of time visible within a fixed structure.
gallery_design_mobile.gallery_design_mobile.06: The section and site studies place interior voids within the larger stone mass, relating the gallery’s orientation and approach to the surrounding landscape.

about_mobile.about_mobile.01: He works with the photograph as both an image and a physical object. Light, sequence and material connect his photographic work with writing and handmade publications.
about_mobile.about_mobile.02: Poetry and prose are published at daipan.ink. The Threes (2025) brings selected writing and images into a handmade book.
about_mobile.about_mobile.03: Working between poetic realism and post-documentary photography, he brings observed scenes into contact with bodily perception and memory. Images and language remain open to one another: a sequence, a printed surface or a pause can shift how a work is read.

in_praise_of_time_mobile.in_praise_of_time_mobile.01: A plant shares the table with cups, containers and traces of use. The photograph holds these ordinary objects together while leaving the gestures that arranged them outside the frame.
in_praise_of_time_mobile.in_praise_of_time_mobile.02: Light falls across a wall and a body in separate places. Their proximity here comes from a passing pattern, allowing the visible surface to become a measure of time. Their pairing holds a correspondence rather than a continuous event. What remains is a brief sensation of contact: light makes unrelated surfaces seem to share a moment, then moves on.
in_praise_of_time_mobile.in_praise_of_time_mobile.03:
Riding wings that beat with the light of night,
alternating lamps flatten my sight,
and I bear the weight of the earth, our mother.
I stand in line inside a dream I made myself, and wake again and again,
as if this were not the world I live in.

Pan, D. (n.d.). A flowing song. daipan.ink.
in_praise_of_time_mobile.in_praise_of_time_mobile.04: The resemblance between the sundae and the sleeping sheep is fleeting. Texture brings them close; a change of scale draws them apart.
in_praise_of_time_mobile.in_praise_of_time_mobile.05: The face returns at a different scale. Recognition gives way to texture, and the slight opening of the lips holds the possibility of a voice. The fragment interrupts the distance established by the preceding scenes, returning attention to the body as the place where time is sensed before it can be named.
in_praise_of_time_mobile.in_praise_of_time_mobile.06: The room offers no clear event, only the position of a body and the worn surfaces around it. Here, stillness begins to feel like accumulated time.
in_praise_of_time_mobile.in_praise_of_time_mobile.07: Gesture brings the body back into view. These encounters belong to different lives; the sequence connects them through pauses, interrupted attention and the light that briefly gathers around a face or a hand.
